  • SCP-0002: Vessel as the whole-Runtime name, Carousel ownership beyond one atomic deduction, and undifferentiated Runtime ownership of the Outcome & Value Store.
  • SCP-0004: Vessel as the complete Runtime and outward product boundary, and ownership of final result assembly.
  • SCP-0006: one undifferentiated Vessel owning the whole live loop. The compiler-only prohibition and deployment neutrality are unchanged.
  • SCP-0011: policy interpretation described as occurring inside a whole-Runtime Vessel. The addressee rules are unchanged.
  • SCP-0014: Vessel ownership of laid-Cable channel execution and data-plane termination.

Decision:

  • The Subsea Cable Runtime is the deployment-neutral whole. It contains the Vessel control plane, the Cable data plane, the Codebase and append-only deduction ledger, the Scheduler and Host ports, and a stateless outward composition layer.
  • The Vessel control plane owns the voyage, the occurrence set, the undeduced frontier, coordination of explicit and speculative structural demand, Touchdown-window accounting, publication of committed structure, and the determination that no structural work remains. It carries no channel frames and owns no Outcome & Value Store.
  • Carousel performs one atomic deduction requested by Vessel: it resolves the occurrence's current alias when applicable, applies its reduction rule with supplied arguments and values, and commits one complete deduction record or none. It does not choose demand, own the frontier, or evaluate leaves.
  • The Cable data plane owns installed topology, input admission and declaration leases, channels and backpressure, routed Values, the Outcome & Value Store, Host emission sessions, multiplicity enforcement, drainage, and terminal propagation. It never reads a mutable alias or creates a deduction record. The Scheduler keeps outcome authority, and the Host keeps primitive, leaf, Anchor, and Host-addressed policy semantics.
  • Vessel publishes each committed result to Cable as one idempotently identified TopologyInstall. Cable exposes none of it as executable until it acknowledges TopologyInstalled; a stale, malformed, or identity-conflicting installation is TopologyInstallRejected and publishes nothing. Until acknowledgement, each newly grounded leaf occupies one pending-install window reservation.
  • A segment's EndOfResult requires both Vessel structural closure and Cable drainage of all installed caused work. EndOfStream additionally requires decommission, closed structural publication, every segment terminal, and full drainage.
  • The final result is assembled by the stateless composition layer from immutable Vessel provenance and Cable completion evidence. Outward adapters attach to that layer, never to plane-private storage.
  • An Agent or operator, never Vessel, authors replanning. After observing authorized Cable output, it may store a new immutable artifact and atomically rebind Name/Arity. Only later-demanded undeduced occurrences observe the new binding; committed deductions and installed topology never change.
  • Process placement never changes alias-observation time, deduction identity, Value order, or terminal semantics.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Modern programming languages ask functions to play two fundamentally different roles.

A function is supposed to describe how a piece of computation is implemented.

Yet, in practice, functions also become the primary mechanism for expressing the dependency structure of a program.

This conflates two independent concerns.

Because functions are treated as value transformations, programmers naturally think in terms of

request  → top-down
response → bottom-up
strict evaluation

Every function call is assumed to immediately invoke another computation and return its result.

As a consequence, the dependency graph of the problem becomes inseparable from the execution strategy chosen by the programmer.

However, these are fundamentally different things.

A program first describes what goals exist and how those goals depend on one another.

Only afterwards should the Runtime decide how those goals are realized, with Scheduler deciding eligibility and outcomes, Host giving grounded leaves concrete meaning, and Cable operating installed data flow.

When separated, the authored program becomes a Voyage Plan whose structural Cable is realized through demand-driven deduction.

Execution order, evaluation strategy, parallelism, batching, cancellation, and cross-occurrence resource ordering belong to Scheduler authority—not to the program. Scheduler controls eligibility, attempts, and scope outcomes; Host-addressed policy may change locality or resource use inside exactly one grounded leaf invocation.

Once this distinction is made, programming changes fundamentally.

Instead of writing execution order, we describe goals.

Instead of manually orchestrating evaluation, we declare dependencies.

Instead of embedding scheduling decisions into business logic, we inject schedulers that implement different execution strategies.

The same program can then execute sequentially, in parallel, lazily, eagerly, locally, remotely, or in a distributed environment without changing its logical structure.

Subsea Cable is built on this separation.

Programs describe dependency structures.

Functions implement grounded Goals. Schedulers decide their eligibility and outcomes. Subsea Cable represents Goals.

A program is not an instruction sequence.

It is a Cable waiting to be laid—committed one deduction at a time while its undeduced aliases remain open to revision.

docs.title: Why Subsea Cable: "How Did I Get Here?"
docs.text:
Subsea Cable attaches intent to every step it takes.

Status of this page

This page explains why Subsea Cable exists and how it differs from other tools. It is an explanatory projection, not a semantic authority. On any difference, follow the sources listed in GOVERNANCE.md, especially the Language Reference. Where a pattern below depends on something not yet decided, the page says so and links the open item.

docs.title: Can you answer this right now?
docs.text:
A long task hits an exception nobody anticipated. Or the context was compacted, or the session dropped and resumed.

  • Which decisions led to the step you are on now?
  • Which of those decisions was wrong?
  • How far back do you need to go, and which effects on the world have already happened since then?

Today an agent answers these questions by rereading its transcript and guessing. It goes back too little and patches a symptom, or, unsure, goes back too far and redoes work that was fine. Adding Airflow or Temporal does not change this. Those engines answer "how do I resume the steps I was given?", not "what was I trying to do when I got here?"

In Subsea Cable, the first question is meant to be a lookup, not an inference. Every committed deduction of a named Goal records the full ArtifactHash it selected and the lineages it extended; an inline Goal-arrow stage takes its identity from the enclosing artifact. The intent behind each grounded leaf is therefore recorded rather than reconstructed. The judgment that remains, deciding which decision was wrong, operates on a small, bounded set of candidates instead of an entire transcript. How much of that record an Agent can query while a voyage is still running is a Runtime capability, described in section 2.

docs.title: The problem: unstructured work is fixed while doing it
docs.text:
Agent work shows what every business already knows: open-ended problems cannot be predicted or modeled cleanly in advance. Three things still hold.

  1. Higher Goals change less. Plans near the leaves are often wrong, but the Goal being pursued and its nearby ancestors are comparatively stable. Most corrections are therefore local, and the natural scope of a correction is the lowest common ancestor that contains both the bad decision and its consequence.
  2. You must be able to try, look, and revise the Goal. Choosing a wrong or unfavorable Goal is not a failure of the method. It is the normal condition of open-ended work.
  3. Revising requires the history so far. Knowing the parent Goal is not enough. To see which decision led to which result, and to redesign exactly that point, you need every leaf reached so far, in order, together with the lineage of each one.

The rarest and most expensive case is when a high-level Goal itself was wrong. History is useful here as well: the evidence for "this Goal was wrong" remains on the Cable with its lineage, so even the decision to change the objective has recorded grounds.

Subsea Cable records this entire structure. Goal definitions are kept as hash-identified artifacts, grounded work is kept as the Cable, and the two are joined through deduction records and lineage. That is why it fits work that has to be corrected while it is being done.

docs.title: Why now: evaluation erases abstraction
docs.text: Evaluation keeps what was computed. Subsea Cable keeps what was intended.

docs.title: "Just call the function" used to be right
docs.text:
The essence of evaluation is erasing abstraction.

  • β-reduction replaces a redex and, at that moment, forgets what the call was for.
  • Graph reduction in Haskell overwrites a thunk with its value and discards the "why".
  • The call stack is the closest thing to a Goal boundary, but a frame is popped the moment it returns.
  • Even when a program is data, as in Lisp, keeping the history is an overhead bolted onto evaluation.

That was reasonable. The executor (the CPU) never needed the "why", and the one who did (the programmer) could reread the code offline. Keeping abstract structure at run time was a cost nobody consumed. Until LLMs started solving open-ended problems the way people do, a deduction whose structure stays visible was a luxury slower than a function call.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
The executor now consumes the "why" itself. To decide what to do next, an LLM needs to know, at run time, "what was I trying to do when I got here?" Abstract structure has turned from a disposable by-product into a run-time input.

The cost argument flipped as well. When a single leaf is an LLM call or an external effect that takes seconds, the cost of maintaining Goal boundaries through deduction is within the noise.

docs.title: Same roots as Haskell, a different purpose
docs.text:
Subsea Cable inherits Haskell's philosophy and was inspired by β-reduction. Its purpose is different.

Haskell Subsea Cable Purpose of reduction Obtain a value Keep Goal boundaries available The reduction process Can be forgotten Is itself the record: each deduction is a commit Replacement Redex is replaced by its result Children are exposed and each lineage is extended Analogy A computation that vanishes when done A call stack that is never popped, whose frames are joined to hash-identified definitions

Subsea Cable's concern is not evaluation. It is being able to keep answering "so what were we trying to do?"

docs.title: The nearest prior work
docs.text:
Self-adjusting computation (Adapton and related systems) keeps the dependency trace of a run and recomputes only what changed when inputs change. Structurally this resembles Cable reuse. The purpose differs.

  • Self-adjusting computation keeps the trace for computational efficiency, and the trace has no intent boundaries.
  • Subsea Cable keeps intent boundaries so that an author, human or agent, can redesign. Reuse is a side benefit.

docs.title: 1.1 Goal definitions: intent fixed by hash
docs.text:
• Every authored Goal definition is stored as an immutable artifact identified by its ArtifactHash.
  • A name is only an alias, a Name/Arity pointer into the Codebase. Changing a definition stores a new artifact and moves the alias.
  • The fact that "at that point, this Goal had this structure" is never lost.

docs.title: 1.2 Deductions and lineage: context on every step
docs.text:
• When a named Goal occurrence is demanded, its reference is resolved and the selected full ArtifactHash, arguments, resulting structure, active lineages, and (for an unqualified reference) the observed Codebase revision are committed together in one deduction record.
  • An inline Goal-arrow stage such as [{code, logs}] -> Diagnose[code, logs] is deduced too, but its record has referenceKind = inline-arrow, no requested name, and no artifact hash: the enclosing artifact supplies its identity, and it adds no lineage segment (Runtime Contract §8.1).
  • A deduction extends each incoming lineage across the edges it commits. Lineage segments are Name/Arity, for example CreateOrder/1.RegisterOrder/1.ValidateStock/1; the hash each segment's occurrence selected lives in that occurrence's deduction record, not in the segment itself.
  • So even a leaf that has already reached Touchdown has a recorded chain of deductions that produced it.
  • When a laid Cable has been decommissioned and drained, a Runtime that claims the voyage-result capability exposes the Fully Touchdown Cable, the ordered list of published grounded leaf hashes, with a provenance index that maps each position back to its deduction ancestry (Runtime Contract §12).

docs.title: 1.3 Joined: one record answers several questions
docs.text:
Question Where the answer comes from Which grounded work is this? Its Touchdown content hash Under which intent was it grounded? Its lineage, joined to the ArtifactHash each named-Goal deduction on that lineage selected Is that intent still current? Compare each recorded ArtifactHash with what its alias resolves to now

Current lineage limitation

Lineage segments identify Goals by Name/Arity. Current analysis must use the recorded artifact hashes alongside those names when aliases change during a voyage. Hash-addressed lineage segments are not available in the current language contract.

docs.title: 2. What this makes possible: replanning after an unexpected failure
docs.text:
The hardest moment for an agent is "this didn't work, and I never considered why." Subsea Cable is designed so that this moment can become a procedure. The steps below are an authoring pattern, not a Runtime algorithm defined by the language, and Vessel never invents a plan change by itself; the agent authors it.

What is portable today, and what needs more

The portable outward Cable surface exposes right-end Values, segment outcomes, diagnostics, and terminals (SCP-0015). It does not expose a failing leaf's own outcome or its deduction ancestry while the Cable is live. Deduction ancestry is composed into the voyage result only after decommission and drainage, and the normalized trace in Runtime Contract §11 is an evidence and profile contract, not a portable live Agent query.

So the walk-back below works after the fact against a drained voyage result from a Runtime that claims voyage-result, followed by a revised new voyage. Doing it mid-voyage requires a Runtime-profile extension or a future contract for live provenance queries; see Open problems.

  1. Observe. Read the segment outcome, diagnostics, and terminal from the outward Cable surface.
  2. Find the cut by walking back. Using the provenance index, walk the reached leaves backward from the failure and inspect each one's deduction ancestry and recorded artifacts. The regression point is the first leaf produced by the deduction that carried the wrong assumption. Choosing that deduction is still a judgment, but you only need to look a short way back, not re-review the whole tree.
  3. Scope with the lowest common ancestor. The common ancestor of the cut and the failure is the smallest scope that contains both the bad decision and its consequence. Its Goal structure ("what we meant to do") and the records after the cut ("what actually happened") are the complete context for replanning.
  4. Revise without rewriting history. Store the revised definition as a new immutable artifact and rebind its alias. Undeduced occurrences observe the new definition when they are demanded; committed deductions never change. If the part to revise is already committed, start a new voyage and reuse unchanged structure from the earlier one (SCP-0004). Structural reuse never by itself permits skipping Host effects.
  5. Keep the abandoned attempt. Nothing is deleted: committed deductions and published Touchdowns stay as history. A $ leaf in that history marks a potential effect boundary, not evidence that an effect happened. Cable membership includes leaves that were withheld, discarded, never dispatched, failed, or cancelled, and Host effects are opaque and never rolled back. Whether an attempt ran, and what it did, comes only from attempt and outcome evidence, or from a separately authorized Outcome Journal.
  6. Bound the loop. Preventing endless regression to the same point is a Scheduler concern expressed through @policy, not a structural one. Concrete policy semantics for this are not defined yet; see Open problems.

docs.title: 3. Compared with the agent loop
docs.text:
An LLM agent loop today is essentially:

while (!done) {
  action = model(transcript)
  result = tool(action)
  transcript.append(action, result)
}
Aspect Current agent loop Subsea Cable Where the plan lives Natural language in the transcript Hash-identified Goal artifacts Execution history Text in the transcript Deduction ledger and the ordered list of reached leaves Link between history and intent None; reread and reinterpret every time Lineage joined to hash-identified artifacts through deduction records Regression point after failure Guessed by reading backward Bounded by walking back through deduction ancestry (after drainage today) Replanning context The whole transcript, too much or missing pieces Lowest-common-ancestor structure plus the records after the cut Effects that may have been applied Depends on memory $ leaves mark where effects could occur; attempt and outcome evidence, or an authorized Outcome Journal, say which ran Resuming after context loss "Where was I?" is guessed Committed deduction records plus the undeduced frontier Context for a sub-agent Summarized by hand A leaf's arguments and its lineage

A transcript does contain both the "why" and the "what". It mixes them as unstructured prose, so they cannot be split or joined mechanically. That is why regression decisions become guesswork.

docs.title: 4.1 How each family records intent and history
docs.text: Family Examples "Why" (intent structure) "What" (execution history) How they are linked Declarative static DAG Airflow, Step Functions, Argo, Dagster A DAG or state-machine definition, pinned per run where the product supports it Task-instance records Per run; no per-occurrence deduction context Code-based durable execution Temporal, Restate Hidden in imperative code, with no address Event history Reconstructed by replay; changing code risks non-determinism Hash-based builds Nix, Bazel Derivation or action graph, by hash Output hashes Linked, but static; no in-run strategy change and no effect model Subsea Cable — Every Goal artifact by hash, plus the realized paths Deduction ledger and published leaves Named-Goal deductions record the selected artifact and lineages; inline stages inherit the enclosing identity; the undeduced frontier stays revisable

docs.title: 4.2 Granularity of "change the plan while it runs"
docs.text: Unit of change Cost Airflow 3 Depends on the DAG bundle: a versioned bundle (for example Git) keeps a run on the bundle version it started with; Local, S3, or GCS bundles can pick up the latest code, and clearing a task may rerun it on the latest bundle version depending on configuration No per-occurrence record of which definition produced which task Step Functions An execution already running keeps the definition it started with Changing the plan means starting a new execution Temporal Versioned branches in workflow code (patching, worker versioning) Developers manage determinism; mistakes surface as non-determinism errors Nix / Bazel The build There is no notion of "during the run" Subsea Cable The occurrence: the past is committed, only the undeduced frontier observes new definitions No replay of authored code; committed records are reused as they are

docs.title: 4.3 The same failure, four ways
docs.text:
"An unexpected exception mid-run. One of the earlier decisions was wrong."

  • Airflow: retry the failed task or rerun the whole DAG. Nothing points at the wrong decision.
  • Temporal: someone must have written the handling code in advance, and the point to return to lives in that author's head.
  • Nix / Bazel: fix the input and rebuild. The cache helps reuse, but changing strategy mid-run is out of scope.
  • Subsea Cable: walk back through deduction ancestry to the cut, scope with the lowest common ancestor, publish a revised artifact, and let the frontier or a new voyage observe it while reusing structure that remains valid. Every step starts from records (after drainage today; live queries are an open item).

docs.title: 5. Why this is hard to substitute
docs.text:
1. Existing tools keep only one of the two records completely, or keep both statically.
    • Static DAGs: the definition exists independently of any run, but its link to execution history is run-level (pinned per run where the product supports it), not per occurrence.
    • Durable execution: the "why" is hidden in code and has no address.
    • Hash builds: both exist, but nothing changes during a run.
    • Agent loops: both are mixed into prose.
  2. Subsea Cable joins the two records through deduction records and still keeps the frontier open. "The past is immutable evidence; the future can be revised from that evidence" holds within one model.
  3. This targets exactly the agent's bottleneck. What agents lack is not durable execution, which existing engines already provide. It is knowing where to start rethinking after a failure, and why. Subsea Cable turns locating that point from inference into lookup.

docs.title: 6. What adopting these guarantees involves
docs.text:
Writing a Goal graph is the beginning. Using it as evidence for replanning means that the record must remain trustworthy when work fails, outputs arrive at different times, and an alias changes while a voyage is live.

What you want from the workflow What the Runtime must keep consistent Revise work that has not committed yet Demand-time alias selection and immutable committed history Explain why a leaf was reached Selected artifacts, occurrences, lineages, and the provenance that joins them Handle parallel or streamed results Value routing, backpressure, multiplicity, and explicit completion Revisit a failed attempt Structural evidence distinguished from actual Host execution and effects

These responsibilities interact. A parser or a successful happy-path demo does not establish them. Choose an implementation by its pinned specification, supported capabilities, reproducible conformance results, and recovery limits. You can spend your integration work on the Voyage Plan and genuine Host leaves while its maintainers verify the execution contract.

The adoption guide describes that boundary. Runtime availability separates dated implementation evidence from the scenarios still in progress. It does not promise an available production release or a delivery date.

docs.title: 7. Open problems
docs.text:
These capabilities are not part of the current portable contract:

  • Live provenance queries. The outward surface does not provide a portable query for a failing leaf's outcome and ancestry while a Cable is live.
  • Lineage-conditioned policies. The language does not define a portable policy that chooses behavior from provenance history.
  • Automatic compensation. Reusing structural evidence does not establish whether a Host effect happened or authorize an undo.
  • Automatic replanning. An Agent or operator authors plan changes; the Runtime does not invent them autonomously.

The specification may describe a workflow pattern before a released Runtime supports it. Check Runtime availability before depending on execution or recovery, and use the adoption guide to prepare a workflow and its explicit Host boundaries.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text:
cases.tsv is the language conformance manifest. Each case names its expected phase and outcome; a conforming implementation must parse every valid and invalid-semantic input, reject every invalid-syntax input, and then produce the listed validation kind for each invalid-semantic input.

DEDUCTION.md contains the complementary Runtime scenarios for demand-time alias resolution, commit atomicity, recovery, occurrence kinds, artifact identity, and the Host boundary. They cannot be expressed by a single source fixture and are normative for a Runtime claiming deduction conformance.

POLICY.md contains the Runtime scenarios for @policy addressee resolution and the Host policy channel. They depend on an attached Scheduler registry and Host capability, so they are stated with test doubles and are normative for a Runtime claiming the policy profile.

LAID_CABLE.md contains the Runtime scenarios for laid Cables, including Vessel-control and Cable-data responsibilities, per-input result segments, Host terminals, and output multiplicity (SCP-0014 and SCP-0015). They need a live channel and Host doubles and are normative for a complete Runtime claiming laid-Cable conformance.

PRIMES_UP_TO.md fixes one reference Voyage Plan and its acceptance oracle for streamed candidate generation, guarded-recursive trial division, Runtime-plane separation, and laid-Cable terminals. The source is also a syntax-accepted fixture in cases.tsv; its end-to-end oracle requires a complete Runtime and the scenario-specific Host implementations described there. It is the acceptance gate for the runnable vertical slice tracked by the streamed-primes runnable demonstration, not an additional requirement for every Runtime that claims general laid-Cable conformance.

docs.title: Required lexical preprocessing
docs.text:
The ANTLR lexer produces physical TERMINATOR, whitespace, and comment tokens. Before parsing, a token-source wrapper must perform this deterministic pass:

  1. Decode the source strictly as UTF-8. Reject malformed input as InvalidSourceEncoding before lexing.
  2. Discard ordinary whitespace and line-comment tokens. The newline following a line comment remains a physical TERMINATOR token.
  3. Replace each block-comment token conceptually with one whitespace boundary. Its internal newlines never produce terminators. Because tokenization has already occurred, discarding the token must not concatenate its neighbors.
  4. Track unmatched opening (, [, and { tokens with a delimiter stack.
  5. For each physical TERMINATOR, suppress it when the delimiter stack is not empty or when the previous significant token is in this exact set:
=  ->  -0>  -1>  -N>  ,  :  @  $
||  &&  ==  !=  <=  >=  <  >
+  -  *  /  %  !
  1. Form named-Goal multiplicity arrows. Track the square-bracket group that begins a Binding right-hand side: the [ immediately following a = at delimiter depth zero. When that group closes back to depth zero and the next three significant tokens are -, one of 0, 1 or N, and > with no intervening character (the end offset of each is immediately followed by the start offset of the next), replace them with one MULTIPLICITY_ARROW token whose text is -0>, -1> or -N> and whose span covers all three. Nowhere else are those tokens fused, so (base)-1>0 and x-1>0 keep their subtraction and comparison, a spaced [x] - 1 > $a is not an arrow, a function-leaf definition (params) -> body has no multiplicity arrow, and an inline Goal-arrow stage has none either.
  2. Form the contextual Root keyword. When the first significant token of a statement (the first of the file, or the first after an emitted logical TERMINATOR, at delimiter depth zero) is the Identifier root and the next significant token is an Identifier, retype it as ROOT. After ROOT, an Identifier, an optional HASH_QUALIFIER, and /, retype a NUMBER with no fractional part as ROOT_ARITY. Every other token is left unchanged, so root = 5 stays a Binding while root A[5], root A/1.0, and start A/1 reach the parser as SyntaxErrors.
  3. Coalesce consecutive surviving physical newlines into one logical TERMINATOR, preserving the span of the coalesced source region.
  4. Emit all other significant tokens unchanged and finally emit EOF. The parser, not this pass, reports unmatched or misordered delimiters.

The “previous significant token” ignores whitespace and comments. A newline before an operator is not continuation; only a newline after a listed token is.

docs.title: Reason and context expectations
docs.text:
cases.tsv records only the stable error kind. For the SCP-0014 output multiplicity fixtures a conforming validator must also report this reason or context:

Fixture Kind Reason or context invalid-semantic/OpaqueHostOutput.vyg OutputMultiplicityCannotBeInferred opaque-host-output invalid-semantic/RecursiveSignatureCycle.vyg OutputMultiplicityCannotBeInferred kind only: recursive-signature-cycle and unknown-conditional-branch both apply invalid-semantic/UnknownConditionalBranch.vyg OutputMultiplicityCannotBeInferred kind only: unknown-conditional-branch and opaque-host-output both apply invalid-semantic/GoalDeclarationMismatch.vyg OutputMultiplicityMismatch goal-declaration, expected /0, actual /1 invalid-semantic/ResolvingMapBranchZero.vyg OutputMultiplicityMismatch resolving-map-branch, expected /1, actual /0 invalid-semantic/ResolvingMapBranchMany.vyg OutputMultiplicityMismatch resolving-map-branch, expected /1, actual /N

Which reason a definition with several causes reports is not yet specified, so those two fixtures check only the kind. A guarded recursive branch always sits beneath a conditional, so no standalone fixture has recursive-signature-cycle as its only cause.

external-symbolic-reference needs an unqualified reference that a Codebase, not the source unit, could later satisfy; a standalone fixture would report GoalNotFound instead. It is covered with the other laid-Cable Runtime scenarios in LAID_CABLE.md.

valid/output-multiplicity.vyg exercises the inference rules that need no explicit arrow: a scalar function leaf (/1), an unkeyed parallel (/0), a resolving Map (/1), all nine cells of the routed serial composition table, an explicit tuple resetting the multiplicity, an absorbing /0 after an opaque upstream, a routed successor of a parallel composite invoked zero times, and a known /0//1 conditional mix inferring /N. Explicit -N> and -0> arrows that agree with the inferred result are accepted. valid/root-contextual-keyword.vyg proves that root remains an ordinary Binding name and that x-1>0 and (root)-1>0 remain expressions.

docs.title: Synchronization rule
docs.text:
Any language change is incomplete until all applicable projections agree:

  • LANGUAGE_REFERENCE.md: structural semantic contract
  • README.md: breadth-first public model and core value
  • SubseaCable.ebnf: implementation-neutral syntax and lexical contract
  • SubseaCable.g4: executable ANTLR4 grammar
  • conformance/cases.tsv and its source files: observable acceptance/rejection
  • conformance/DEDUCTION.md: observable demand-time deduction behavior
  • conformance/POLICY.md: observable policy addressee and Host-channel behavior
  • conformance/LAID_CABLE.md: observable laid-Cable channel, segment, terminal, and multiplicity behavior

The ANTLR grammar must generate without warnings or errors, generated Java must compile against the matching ANTLR runtime, every syntax-valid case must reach EOF without lexer/parser errors after preprocessing, and every syntax-invalid case must produce at least one lexer/parser error. Semantic cases require the stable error kind listed in the manifest.

The current grammar has been generation-checked with ANTLR 4.13.2. Generated artifacts are build output and are not committed.

CI reproduces the syntax half of this check on every pull request with .github/scripts/grammar/check_cases.py: it generates the Python parser with -Werror, applies the reference preprocessor in .github/scripts/grammar/preprocess.py, and requires every cases.tsv row to parse or fail as listed. Run it locally with python .github/scripts/grammar/check_cases.py --antlr-jar <antlr-4.13.2-complete.jar> after pip install antlr4-python3-runtime==4.13.2. It does not check semantic kinds; those remain the implementer's conformance obligation.

docs.title: Deduction Conformance Scenarios
docs.text:
These scenarios specify observable Runtime behavior that syntax-only .vyg fixtures cannot express. They are normative for implementations claiming the demand-time alias and deduction profile.

For every scenario, an artifact is immutable after storage, alias updates are atomic, and a successful deduction record contains the occurrence ID, requested name and arity, selected full artifact hash, observed codebase revision, arguments, result structure, and active lineages.

Under SCP-0014 a scenario that "demands the Root occurrence" of Name/n lays that target, sends the stated input, and demands the Root occurrence of that one input segment. Goals whose bodies reference Goals stored by another unit declare their output multiplicity explicitly, because inference never consults a mutable alias. Laid-Cable channel, terminal, and multiplicity scenarios are in LAID_CABLE.md.

docs.title: 1. Parent deduction does not resolve a child
docs.text:
1. Store B/0 as hash-b1 and bind alias B/0 -> hash-b1.
  2. Store Upper = [] -1> B[] as Upper/0 and demand the Root occurrence of Upper/0. (A Goal-arrow body reference always carries [...] or (...); a bare B is valid only as a composition stage.)
  3. The committed Upper deduction exposes a child occurrence containing symbolic B/0; that child has no selected artifact hash yet.
  4. Rebind B/0 -> hash-b2.
  5. Demand the child B occurrence.

The B deduction MUST select hash-b2, not hash-b1.

docs.title: 2. A committed occurrence never retargets
docs.text:
1. Bind B/0 -> hash-b1.
  2. Demand occurrence b-occurrence; it commits hash-b1.
  3. Rebind B/0 -> hash-b2.
  4. Demand b-occurrence again.

The Runtime MUST reuse its committed deduction record and MUST NOT resolve the alias again.

docs.title: 3. Separate occurrences can observe separate revisions
docs.text:
1. Create two distinct unqualified B/0 occurrences.
  2. With B/0 -> hash-b1, demand the first occurrence.
  3. Rebind B/0 -> hash-b2.
  4. Demand the second occurrence.

The first deduction MUST retain hash-b1; the second MUST select hash-b2. The occurrences remain distinct even if their arguments and lineages happen to match.

docs.title: 4. Hash-qualified references stay pinned
docs.text:
1. Store an occurrence authored as B#<prefix-of-hash-b1>[].
  2. Prepare its containing artifact, resolving the prefix to full hash-b1.
  3. Rebind the human-readable B/0 alias to hash-b2.
  4. Demand the qualified occurrence.

The deduction MUST select hash-b1. It MUST NOT consult the current alias.

docs.title: 5. Intermediate deductions are checkpoints
docs.text:
1. Demand a composite Goal that exposes a descendant Goal but does not yet demand that descendant.
  2. Persist the successful parent deduction record.
  3. Interrupt and resume the run.

The Runtime MUST restore the parent as committed and the descendant as undeduced. Touchdown is not required for the parent deduction to be a durable structural checkpoint.

docs.title: 6. Failed deduction is atomic
docs.text:
Force a failure during alias lookup, dynamic routing, cycle detection, or Host primitive evaluation before a deduction can finish.

The Runtime MUST NOT retain a partial successful deduction record or expose partially committed children. Earlier deduction records remain unchanged.

docs.title: 7. Primitive semantics belongs to the Host
docs.text: Deduce A = [x] -1> B[x + 1] under an identified Host primitive-semantics profile. Carousel requests x + 1 from that Host capability. No Goal node, leaf, or Scheduler work is created for the operator expression. The successful value and Host profile identity are recorded with the deduction.

docs.title: 8. Both leaf forms cross the Host boundary
docs.text:
Ground one arrow-function leaf and one $Anchor leaf. The Scheduler offers both to the Host:

  • the Host evaluates the validated arrow-function body;
  • the Host resolves and invokes the Anchor identifier.

The Anchor registry is only one Host capability; it is not the whole Host.

docs.title: 9. Conditional deduction exposes only the selected branch
docs.text:
Validate and store the following while both A/0 and B/0 aliases exist:

Choose = [flag] -1> [
    flag,
    {
        true: A[],
        false: B[],
    },
]

Remove the current B/0 alias, then lay Choose/1, send the input true, and demand its Root occurrence. Carousel MUST evaluate the selector through Host primitive semantics, commit the selected key, and expose one symbolic A/0 child. It MUST NOT create a B/0 occurrence, resolve that alias, or report GoalNotFound for the unselected branch. Structural validation still checks the authored branch form and statically available arity information. ConditionalBranchSelected MUST record the selector's stable value slot, canonical digest, selected normalized key, and active primitive profile. Even though the selected A/0 edge is non-recursive, speculative replenishment MAY expose the symbolic child but MUST NOT deduce it; an explicit Scheduler demand is required to cross the committed conditional branch edge.

docs.title: 10. Guarded recursion creates fresh occurrences
docs.text: Lay CountDown/1 from conformance/valid/conditional-recursion.vyg, send the input 2, and demand its Root occurrence. After each selection, explicitly demand the exposed recursive child. Successive demands MUST expose distinct occurrences for CountDown[1], CountDown[0], and Done[]. The three CountDown/1 occurrences MAY share one GoalNodeId, but each MUST retain its own arguments, lineage, alias observation, and immutable deduction record. No edge points back to an ancestor occurrence. Prefetch MUST NOT cross any of the committed conditional branch edges without those explicit demands.

docs.title: 11. Recursive steps retain demand-time alias behavior
docs.text:
1. Demand a guarded recursive occurrence far enough to expose, but not demand, its next symbolic recursive child.
  2. Rebind the recursive Goal's Name/Arity alias to a new artifact that preserves a compatible guarded form.
  3. Demand the child.

The child MUST select the new hash. The parent and every earlier recursive step retain their committed hashes. Guarded recursion never pins all future steps at the first occurrence.

docs.title: 12. A valid recursive voyage may not terminate
docs.text: Use a guarded recursive Goal whose selector never chooses its authored exit for the supplied input. Validation and deduction MUST NOT report CycleDetected merely because the same Goal definition is selected repeatedly. Each selected step commits normally only after explicit Scheduler demand. Speculative replenishment MUST stop at each exposed conditional child even while the Touchdown window is empty and even when local analysis did not classify the selected edge as recursive. An explicit deduction-work budget may pause the demand sequence and Scheduler policy may cancel the voyage. Every completed record remains immutable and no synthetic exit or partial deduction is permitted.

docs.title: 13. An unresolved selector crosses no value barrier
docs.text:
1. Create a conditional occurrence whose selector depends on an unresolved routed output from an earlier Host leaf.
  2. Explicitly demand the conditional occurrence before that output resolves.
  3. Resolve the output and demand the same occurrence again.

Step 2 MUST report DeductionBlocked(pendingValue), commit no deduction, select no key, create no branch occurrence or alias observation, and emit no ConditionalBranchSelected. A speculative pass reports the corresponding PrefetchBlocked reason. Step 3 evaluates the selector and commits exactly one selected branch atomically.

docs.title: 14. Late alias cycles distinguish guarded re-entry
docs.text:
Create a demanded unqualified occurrence whose alias resolves to a GoalNodeId already on its ancestor chain.

  • With no committed conditional branch selection between the ancestor and the explicitly demanded occurrence, deduction MUST fail atomically with CycleDetected.
  • Reaching that same unguarded re-entry during speculative replenishment MUST instead abandon the path silently: no occurrence, no CycleDetected, and no other diagnostic. Demanding it afterwards MUST report CycleDetected, so the diagnostic does not depend on the prefetch target.
  • With at least one committed conditional selection on that path, Carousel MUST allow a fresh occurrence. It MUST NOT reuse the ancestor occurrence or create a back-edge.

docs.title: 15. Conditional reuse requires selector-value evidence
docs.text: Record a conditional deduction that selected _, then start a later voyage whose corresponding selector produces a different value that also selects _. The two ConditionalBranchSelected events have the same selected key but different canonical selector-value digests. The later voyage MUST NOT reuse the earlier selected-branch segment. Reuse is permitted only when the stable value slot, digest, primitive profile, and every other SCP-0004 dependency fingerprint match.

docs.title: 16. A Host value unblocks later deduction
docs.text:
Use a serial route whose first grounded leaf produces a value explicitly routed into a later Goal occurrence. Demand the later occurrence before the Host outcome exists. Carousel MUST report DeductionBlocked(pendingValue), commit no downstream deduction, and leave every downstream unqualified reference symbolic.

Complete the leaf with Succeeded(value) and let Cable accept that output into its Outcome & Value Store. Demanding the same downstream occurrence again with every other prerequisite unchanged MUST read the resolved routed value and commit its deduction. The earlier leaf and every deduction preceding the barrier remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

docs.title: 17. Host evaluation cannot choose or rewrite Goal topology
docs.text:
Snapshot the Deduction Ledger immediately before dispatching a grounded leaf to a recording Host. The Host-facing surface MUST expose no operation that edits a deduction, resolves a Goal alias, selects a conditional branch, or publishes a Touchdown. After the Host returns a typed outcome, the current ledger MUST equal the snapshot; only Cable-owned outcome/value state and trace may change.

If the returned value later participates in routing or a conditional selector, topology changes only when Vessel sends Carousel a separate exact demand, Carousel commits the affected reduction, and Cable atomically installs the published slice. The Host return itself MUST NOT create that structure or rewrite any earlier record.

docs.title: 18. Deployment topology preserves the Runtime boundary
docs.text:
Run the same Voyage Plan twice against deterministic Host doubles: once through an in-process adapter and once through an out-of-process adapter. Fix the Codebase revision, Scheduler profile and demand sequence, primitive profile, Host outcomes, and routed values.

Normalize each trace by removing transport-only events and fields, timestamps, and durations; replace runId with one fixed token; map every runtime occurrence ID to its root-to-leaf child-ordinal vector; and map each attempt ID to its normalized occurrence plus attempt ordinal. The two normalized traces MUST have the same semantic boundary-event multiset and the same causal order within each occurrence: Touchdown publication precedes Scheduler eligibility and dispatch, which precede the Host outcome, value resolution, and any resumed Carousel demand that consumes that value. No global order is required between independent occurrences unless the fixed Runtime/Carousel profile supplies one.

After applying the same identity normalization, the selected hashes, arguments, reduction results, observed codebase revisions, and lineages in their deduction records MUST be equal. Their ordered segment outcomes and Fully Touchdown Cables MUST also be equal. Process placement MUST NOT move alias resolution, policy interpretation, topology selection, or outcome ownership across their specified component boundaries.

docs.title: 19. An inline Goal-arrow stage is its own occurrence
docs.text:
Use a serial route whose second stage is an inline Goal-arrow stage that destructures a routed map, for example [Collect[], [{code, logs}] -> Diagnose[code, logs]].

Demand the stage before Collect produces its output. The stage MUST remain undeduced under the conservative value barrier, report DeductionBlocked(pendingValue) on explicit demand, and commit nothing. It MUST be exposed with occurrenceKind = goal-arrow-stage.

Resolve the output and demand the stage again. It MUST commit exactly one deduction record with referenceKind = inline-arrow, the parameter arity, no requested name and no artifact hash. Its Diagnose child MUST carry the enclosing Goal's lineage with no segment added for the stage, and MUST sit one child-ordinal segment deeper than the stage, so every descendant leaf's root-to-leaf ordinal vector includes the stage's ordinal.

Supply a routed value that does not match the stage's pattern instead: the stage MUST fail with a deduction-phase DestructureMismatch and commit no partial record.

docs.title: 20. NoOutput where a value is required
docs.text:
Run four variants:

  1. a /0 leaf, or a /N leaf that emits no Value before its terminal, whose edge is routed into a later occurrence;
  2. a /1 leaf that completes successfully with no Value while routed into a later occurrence;
  3. a legacy/internal NoOutput as the result of a resolving-map branch that is being bound, where no declared branch multiplicity has already rejected the structure;
  4. a legacy/internal NoOutput in a value position inside a function-leaf body.

Variant 1 is not an error: the later occurrence is invoked zero times and the segment ends with EndOfResult(Succeeded). Variant 2 MUST report host-phase OutputMultiplicityMismatch(expected = /1, context = host-emission), not NoOutputNotRoutable. Variant 3 MUST report deduction-phase NoOutputNotRoutable, and variant 4 MUST report host-phase NoOutputNotRoutable. Each failure is scoped to the failing occurrence: no earlier committed deduction changes, and no partial record is retained. A leaf that returns NoOutput where no value is required is not an error.

docs.title: 21. Structure-valued lookup maps select one entry
docs.text:
Store conformance/valid/structure-valued-lookup-map.vyg, lay Pick/1, and send the input "left". Exactly one entry participates: the Left[] occurrence is created and the other entries create no occurrence, resolve no alias, and observe no value.

Send the input "missing" to a Cable laid from a copy of the map with the _ entry removed. When the key is statically known the miss is a validation error; when it is only known at demand time it MUST be a deduction-phase KeyNotFound. With the _ entry present, the same demand MUST select the wildcard entry.

A selected entry receives no implicit upstream value: a stage preceding the lookup MUST NOT be routed into the entry unless the entry says so.

docs.title: 22. Artifact identity captures the values a term names
docs.text:
1. Store two units whose Goals are textually identical but which read different top-level values. Their ArtifactHash values MUST differ.
  2. Edit a top-level value that no Goal in the unit references by name. Every ArtifactHash in the unit MUST be unchanged. 2b. The capture is transitive, not direct-only. Bind b to a value, bind a to a value that references b by name, and write a Goal whose term references only a. Change b. That Goal's ArtifactHash MUST change. An implementation that captures only directly referenced bindings passes every other scenario here and fails this one, which is the point of the case. 2c. Canonical order is a contract. Reorder the top-level binding declarations without changing any value. Because top-level bindings form one order-independent scope and the closure is captured in canonical order, every ArtifactHash in the unit MUST be unchanged.
  3. Store a unit whose Goal selects from a structure-valued lookup map, then rebind a Name/Arity alias that one of the map's entries references. The referencing artifact's ArtifactHash MUST be unchanged, and a later occurrence selecting that entry MUST observe the new binding.
  4. Edit the map's own structure — add, remove, or reshape an entry. The referencing artifact's ArtifactHash MUST change.

docs.title: 23. Agent-authored rebind changes only the open future
docs.text:
In one active input segment, demand occurrence B1 while B/1 names artifact H1. Commit its deduction. Then expose an authorized early Cable Value or outcome to an Agent test double. The Agent stores immutable artifact H2 and atomically rebinds B/1 through Vessel's Codebase-facing control surface before a later distinct occurrence B2 is demanded.

B1 MUST remain committed to H1; neither its record nor installed topology changes. B2 MUST atomically observe and commit H2. The two records MAY show different Codebase revisions within the same segment. Vessel MUST NOT create H2 or move the alias without the authorized Agent operation.

Make the rebind and B2 demand concurrent. The deduction's atomic alias read MUST linearize with the rebind and commit exactly one complete revision/hash, never a mixture or retry-selected second hash.

Repeat the update twice with no concurrent demand: first submit an artifact that fails validation, then submit an otherwise valid artifact with a stale expectedRevision. Each update MUST fail atomically. Neither may store a validated replacement as the current B/1 target, change any committed deduction, or alter any installed topology. A later distinct demand MUST still resolve B/1 to the previously installed alias target.

docs.title: 24. Cable cannot deduce and Vessel cannot synthesize data
docs.text:
Exercise the control and data planes through test ports that expose all calls. Cable MUST make no Codebase alias lookup, apply no reduction, and write no deduction record. Vessel MUST carry no channel frame and MUST NOT synthesize a Value, outcome, EndOfResult, or EndOfStream without Cable evidence.

When a deduction is blocked on one routed slot, Vessel MUST request that exact resolved slot from Cable and pass its value to Carousel. Carousel MUST make no direct Cable query or scan. Removing either permitted port call keeps the occurrence blocked rather than moving the responsibility into another plane.

docs.title: 25. Topology installation is atomic, idempotent, and gates Touchdown
docs.text:
Commit a reduction result containing at least one grounded leaf, then delay Cable's installation acknowledgement.

  • Before acknowledgement, no part of the slice is executable, no Touchdown is visible to Scheduler, and the leaf is absent from the Fully Touchdown Cable.
  • Each grounded leaf occupies exactly one pending-install window reservation; acknowledgement delay permits no additional speculative demand.
  • Re-sending the same installId and identical content yields the same TopologyInstalled acknowledgement, one installed slice, one publication, and no duplicate reservation.
  • Reusing the identity with different content yields TopologyInstallRejected(identity-conflict); sending to a terminated segment yields TopologyInstallRejected(stale-segment). Neither installs or publishes anything.
  • Sending an incomplete slice or one inconsistent with already installed topology yields TopologyInstallRejected(malformed-slice). No fragment is installed, no occurrence or Touchdown is published, and no executable topology becomes visible.

On successful acknowledgement the reservation becomes one published, unconsumed Touchdown without changing speculation occupancy. For an explicit demand, DemandedTouchdownOverTarget is decided when deduction commit creates the reservations, using published unconsumed Touchdowns plus pending-install reservations. The later acknowledgement only converts the reservation and MUST NOT emit or re-evaluate that diagnostic.

Delay an installation, then exercise three terminal paths: unrecoverable segment failure, segment cancellation, and decommission/drain completion. In each case the reservation MUST remain occupied until the recorded terminal linearizes and makes later installation or publication impossible, then be released exactly once. A request or transient failure before terminalization MUST NOT release it.

docs.title: 26. Process placement preserves the plane protocol
docs.text:
Repeat Section 18 with the Vessel/Carousel and Cable data plane first in one process and then separated by a transport. Extend normalization only by removing transport-local send/receive events and replacing installation IDs with their stable logical identity.

The normalized StructuralDemand, deduction commit, TopologyInstall, TopologyInstalled, Touchdown publication, Value, outcome, and terminal order MUST match. Alias observation, policy interpretation, outcome authority, and final-result membership MUST stay with the same logical owners. Delaying a split-process acknowledgement MUST NOT change speculative demand count or overshoot diagnostics.

docs.title: Laid-Cable Conformance Scenarios
docs.text:
These scenarios specify observable Subsea Cable Runtime behavior across the Vessel control plane and Cable data plane for laid Cables, per-input result segments, terminals, and Goal output multiplicity defined by SCP-0014. Plane ownership and the completion handshake additionally follow SCP-0015. A single source fixture cannot express them. They need a live Cable, deterministic Host doubles, and a controllable Scheduler, and they are normative for an implementation claiming laid-Cable conformance.

Every scenario uses the outward operations lay(goalRef), send(cable, input), and decommision(cable). They are Runtime operations, not Voyage syntax, and lay always takes a named Name/inputArity reference: composite structure is laid through a named wrapper Goal, never as an anonymous arrow. Unless a scenario says otherwise, the Codebase holds this unit:

P = [x] -N> $p(x)
Q = [x] -1> $q(x)
Z = [x] -0> $z(x)
S = [v] -0> $sink(v)

PThenQ = [x] -> [P[x], Q]
PThenS = [x] -> [P[x], S]
QThenS = [x] -> [Q[x], S]
ZThenQ = [x] -> [Z[x], Q]
Fan    = [x] -> {Q[x], P[x]}

root PThenQ/1

$p, $q, $z, and $sink are deterministic, recording Host doubles whose emissions, terminals, delays, and failures each scenario programs. The bracketed identifiers after each heading are stable coverage identifiers: plain numbers cover the laid-Cable decisions of SCP-0014, and R numbers cover the Runtime-plane decisions of SCP-0015. Identifiers satisfied by source fixtures are mapped in the final section.

docs.title: 1. Host result multiplicity  [1, 2, 3, 4, 60]
docs.text:
Lay Z/1, Q/1, and P/1 and send one input to each.

  • Z succeeds with no Value: the right end observes only EndOfResult(Succeeded).
  • Q emits one Value: the right end observes that Value and then EndOfResult(Succeeded).
  • P emits zero, one, and three Values in three separate segments; each is followed by exactly one EndOfResult(Succeeded).

Then lay QThenS/1 and ZThenQ/1 so each violation has downstream work:

  • $q emits one Value and then a second. The second MUST be rejected before routing. S MUST run exactly once, for the first Value, and that run and its effects are not rolled back. Only after that S run terminates does the segment emit exactly one EndOfResult(Failed(OutputMultiplicityMismatch( expected = /1, context = host-emission))).
  • $q completes successfully with zero Values: S runs zero times and the segment emits exactly one failed EndOfResult with the same diagnostic.
  • $z emits a Value: it MUST be rejected before routing, Q runs zero times, and the segment emits exactly one EndOfResult(Failed(OutputMultiplicityMismatch( expected = /0, context = host-emission))).

docs.title: 2. /N Host terminals [5, 61, 62]
docs.text:
Lay PThenS/1 and program $p:

  1. Emit two Values, a successful Host terminal, then a third Value.
  2. Emit one Value and two successful terminals.
  3. As variant 1, but make the second S run fail.
  4. Emit one Value and return normally with no terminal.

The first terminal seals the emission session. In variants 1–3 the late Value MUST be rejected before routing and recorded as HostTerminalProtocolViolation(kind = late-value), and the second terminal MUST be recorded as kind = duplicate-terminal. Neither changes the successful Host emission result nor creates a second EndOfResult. S runs once per accepted Value, and the segment's single outward EndOfResult follows only after those runs drain: Succeeded in variants 1 and 2, Failed in variant 3, showing that the Host terminal did not fix the segment outcome. In variant 4 S MUST run once for the accepted Value and finish, and then the segment emits exactly one EndOfResult(Failed(HostTerminalProtocolViolation(kind = missing-terminal))).

docs.title: 3. Silence is not termination  [6]
docs.text: Lay P/1, send an input, and let the Host double stay connected without emitting. The segment MUST remain pending indefinitely; no EndOfResult, NoOutput, or success is inferred. With @timeout authored on the leaf, the Scheduler policy ends it with the corresponding non-success outcome.

docs.title: 4. One active input segment  [7, 15, 33, 35]
docs.text:
Lay PThenQ/1 and send two inputs before the first segment ends.

  • No occurrence of the second segment is disclosed, deduced, prefetched, alias-resolved, or dispatched until the first segment's EndOfResult has propagated and its caused work has drained.
  • No Value, attempt outcome, or routed binding from one segment satisfies an occurrence, value barrier, or binding in the other.
  • Cable-level state (queue, buffers, lifecycle) is inspectably separate from each segment's Outcome & Value Store and deduction namespace.

docs.title: 5. Immediate intra-segment flow and per-Value routing  [8, 39, 40, 41, 45]
docs.text: Lay PThenQ/1 where $p emits 10, 20, 30 with a controllable delay between them. Q MUST be invoked for 10 before P emits 20. Exactly three complete Q/1 evaluations occur in FIFO order and the composite is /N. When P emits nothing, Q is invoked zero times and the segment succeeds. No first-Value selection, collection, or multiplicity failure occurs.

docs.title: 6. Authored sinks  [9]
docs.text:
Store this unit and lay PrintPrimes/1:

PrintPrimes = [limit] -> [Eratosthenes[limit], PrintPrime]
PrintPrime  = [prime] -0> $PrintLn(prime)
Eratosthenes = [limit] -N> $eratosthenes(limit)
root PrintPrimes/1

Send 20. One PrintPrime/1 and one $PrintLn invocation MUST occur per prime, each visible as its own occurrence with its own outcome. The segment's EndOfResult MUST wait until all of them terminate. No cable Voyage variable exists and no terminal frame is passed as an Anchor argument.

docs.title: 7. Decommission and EndOfStream [10, 50, 63]
docs.text:
Lay the plan's default target PThenQ/1, send three inputs, make the second fail, then call decommision.

  • A later send MUST return AdmissionClosed and consume no Input(k).
  • All three accepted segments drain, including the one after the failure.
  • EndOfStream is emitted once, after the final EndOfResult, and carries no aggregate outcome.
  • Race a send against decommision many times. Exactly the sends whose admission commit wins receive contiguous ordinals; each loser releases any pins it acquired and returns AdmissionClosed. A send blocked in a slow pin attempt before admission MUST NOT delay EndOfStream.

docs.title: 8. Full tuple binding and routing shorthand  [11, 16, 46]
docs.text:
• [A, B] with a unary B routes each A Value into B; no other arity has a bare shorthand.
  • [A, B[y]]: A is still demanded and evaluated, its effects, Touchdowns, outcome, and provenance remain observable, and only its routed Values are discarded. B is invoked once with its written tuple, and the composite takes B's multiplicity even when A is /N.
  • No written argument list is ever completed from an upstream Value.

docs.title: 9. Multiplicity and identity  [12]
docs.text: Store F = [x] -1> $f(x) and a variant F = [x] -N> $f(x) in successive codebase revisions. Their StructureHash values, and therefore GoalNodeId, MUST differ. Publishing both under F/1 in one revision MUST be rejected: an alias key is Name/inputArity only, and multiplicity is never an overload axis. A memo key containing GoalNodeId distinguishes the two.

docs.title: 10. Emission positions  [13, 14]
docs.text: Let P emit three equal payloads. Their downstream occurrences MUST carry Emission(0), Emission(1), Emission(2) position segments. The payloads are unchanged and carry no ordinal. Repeat with the Host completing downstream work in reverse order; the Fully Touchdown Cable order MUST be identical, following tagged Authored(k) and Emission(k) positions (Authored before Emission at a common parent) rather than completion timing.

docs.title: 11. Adapter surface  [19]
docs.text: Every TUI, MCP, library, and service adapter MUST expose arbitrary-Goal debugging only as lay(goalRef) plus separate send and decommission operations. None may expose evaluate(goal, arguments) or an equivalent that combines lay, send, and an implicit decommision.

docs.title: 12. Parallel composite terminal  [20, 43]
docs.text: Lay Fan/1. The right end MUST observe no Value and exactly one EndOfResult carrying the Scheduler-determined scope outcome. Branch terminals remain internal regardless of their arrival order.

docs.title: 13. Channel capacity  [21, 22, 23]
docs.text: Run scenario 5 with capacity 0, 1, and the profile default. Values, terminals, outcomes, and the Fully Touchdown Cable MUST be identical; only blocking may differ. A Host send that blocks on a full channel remains one active attempt, never reclassified as undispatched. Touchdown prefetch and channel capacity each enforce their own bound: shrinking one does not relax the other.

docs.title: 14. Admission pins  [24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29]
docs.text:
• lay alone creates no segment and pins nothing.
  • Each accepted send pins the Scheduler registry, Host capability profile, and forwarding allowlist before any disclosure or deduction for its segment.
  • A send whose pin fails returns ProfileNegotiationFailed and produces no segment, occurrence, Cable member, or EndOfResult.
  • Change a declaration between two sends: the segments record different immutable pin sets.
  • A queued admitted segment keeps its snapshots resolvable until its terminal propagates, with no repinning when it activates. An attempt to evict a pinned snapshot is reported as a Runtime contract violation. A Host endpoint outage under a retained pin is an ordinary attempt failure.

docs.title: 15. Demand-time alias per segment  [30, 31, 32, 34]
docs.text: Lay unqualified Root/1, send an input, rebind Root/1, then send another. The later segment MUST select the artifact visible when its own Root occurrence is demanded. A queued segment observes no alias before it becomes active. Rebinding never changes an already deduced occurrence. A shared ledger backend keeps each segment's deduction namespace distinct.

docs.title: 16. Input provenance and the final result  [36, 37, 38, 47, 48, 49]
docs.text:
Lay PThenQ/1 and send four inputs where the second is rejected (arity) and the third fails.

  • The admitted inputs receive Input(0), Input(1), Input(2); the rejected send has no ordinal.
  • The same inner occurrence path in two segments stays distinct through its Input(k) prefix.
  • The Fully Touchdown Cable concatenates segment lists in increasing Input(k) order. The ordinal appears in no control frame and no Touchdown content hash.
  • The failed segment keeps its published Values, effects, deduction records, and Touchdowns, and the following segment starts normally after the failed terminal propagates and drains.
  • The final result contains one SegmentOutcome(Input(k), outcome) per admitted input, in ordinal order.

docs.title: 17. Empty routed segments  [17, 18]
docs.text: Lay ZThenQ/1, and lay PThenQ/1 with $p emitting no Value before its terminal: in both, Q MUST be invoked zero times and the segment ends EndOfResult(Succeeded) with no NoOutputNotRoutable. Lay QThenS/1 with $q succeeding with no Value: S runs zero times and the segment MUST fail with OutputMultiplicityMismatch(context = host-emission), not NoOutputNotRoutable.

docs.title: 18. Resolving-map branches after alias resolution  [53, 54]
docs.text: Store Both = [x] -> {a: Q[x], b: R[x]} while R/1 is /1, then rebind R/1 to a /N artifact before the branch is demanded. Demanding it MUST report deduction-phase OutputMultiplicityMismatch(context = resolving-map-branch) before Host dispatch. The rebound /N branch stays invalid even when the Host double would emit exactly one Value; no first Value is chosen and no key is omitted.

docs.title: 19. Unresolved external references  [56, 57]
docs.text:
In a Codebase where Ext/1 is stored by another unit:

  • W = [x] -> Ext[x] in a new unit MUST report OutputMultiplicityCannotBeInferred(reason = external-symbolic-reference). Inference MUST NOT consult the current Ext/1 alias.
  • W = [x] -1> Ext[x] is accepted without resolving Ext/1. If Ext/1 later resolves to a /N artifact, demanding the occurrence MUST report deduction-phase OutputMultiplicityMismatch(context = goal-declaration) before Host dispatch.
  • W = [x] -> [Ext[x], Z] infers /0 without resolving Ext/1.

docs.title: 20. Hash-qualified Root target  [58]
docs.text:
1. Store Main = [x] -1> $main(x) as Main/1 → hash-m1.
  2. Store a Voyage Plan whose Root is root Main#<prefix of hash-m1>/1. The prefix MUST expand to the full hash-m1 when the plan is stored, exactly as for a hash-qualified Goal reference.
  3. Rebind the Main/1 alias to a new artifact hash-m2.
  4. Lay the stored plan's default target, send 7, and demand the Root occurrence.

The Root occurrence MUST select hash-m1 without consulting the current Main/1 alias, and the declaration itself MUST NOT have created any occurrence or deduction before the send. Repeat with an unqualified root Main/1: the Root occurrence then selects hash-m2, the artifact visible at its demand. A prefix that matches no stored artifact MUST fail validation with HashNotFound, and one that matches several with AmbiguousHashPrefix.

docs.title: 21. lay creates the voyage/Cable pair before returning [R15]
docs.text: Call lay(P/1) and instrument both planes. The operation MUST return its opaque CableHandle only after Vessel's voyage and Cable's data-plane lifecycle both exist. At return there is still no admitted segment, pin/lease, occurrence, deduction, Host work, or alias observation. Failure to create either half returns no usable handle and leaves no half-live public Cable.

docs.title: 22. Segment activation reuses Cable declaration leases  [R14]
docs.text: Admit one input with pinned Scheduler registry, Host capability, and forwarding allowlist identities. When the segment becomes active, Cable supplies its input tuple and immutable lease references to Vessel. Vessel MUST create the Root occurrence from those leases and perform no second pin or registry negotiation. Replacing a registry after admission affects no active or queued segment whose lease was already accepted.

docs.title: 23. Scheduler and Host projections cross Cable correctly  [R13]
docs.text: Attach Scheduler-addressed scope policy and Host-addressed leaf policy in one segment. BeforeAttempt, Hold, ChildScopeOutcome, and equivalent scope events MUST reach Scheduler only. After Scheduler authorizes a leaf, Host MUST receive hostPolicies[] only and MUST never receive directPolicies[] or the Cable handle. Storing Scheduler-determined outcomes in Cable MUST NOT let Cable choose or reinterpret them.

docs.title: 24. Structural closure and drainage are both required  [R9, R11]
docs.text:
Run four variants:

  1. Cable has drained installed work but one reachable undeduced occurrence is ready and Scheduler withholds it.
  2. Vessel reports no reachable structural work but one installed Host emission or downstream channel operation remains active.
  3. A conditional branch is unselected, or /0/empty /N creates no downstream invocation.
  4. Both structural closure and Cable drainage are true.

Variants 1 and 2 MUST emit no EndOfResult; silence is not completion. Variant 1 remains pending until Scheduler demands the occurrence or makes an accepted terminal decision. Variant 3 creates no reachable frontier for the absent path. Variant 4 linearizes exactly one segment terminal. After decommision, EndOfStream additionally waits for Vessel to close topology publication and for Cable to propagate every segment terminal and drain every channel/attempt.

docs.title: 25. Final composition cannot bypass a plane  [R17]
docs.text:
Complete the same multi-segment Cable with a same-process and split-process Runtime. Vessel supplies immutable deduction/position provenance; Cable supplies completed segment order and drainage evidence. The stateless Runtime composition layer MUST produce identical Fully Touchdown Cable membership, order, and ordered SegmentOutcome values in both profiles.

An outward adapter that reads Vessel or Cable private storage directly instead of the two immutable result ports is non-conforming, even if its example output happens to match.
